lesson 01 SQL foundations · beginner

Meet your first SELECT

Choose columns and read rows from a table.

THE IDEA

A table is a set of rows with named columns. SELECT lists the columns you want; FROM names the table that holds them. In Retail, every row of customers is one identified wholesale customer and every row of products is one stock code. A query reads rows; it never changes them. Worked steps sometimes end with LIMIT so you only preview a few rows. LIMIT is not part of the pattern, and nothing grades it until its own lesson.

DATASET: RETAIL

customers
4 columns · 848 rows
products
6 columns · 5,304 rows

WORKED EXAMPLE

The step marked “the pattern” is what the challenges build on. Running examples doesn’t count toward progress.

1

See a few customers. Run this first. Each row is one customer. LIMIT 10 only shortens the preview; the challenges ask for every row.

step-1.sql
Run
sql›
SELECT *
FROM customers
LIMIT 10;
2

Keep only the columns you need. Same customers, but SELECT now lists just two columns—the ones you ask for.the pattern

example.sql
Run
sql›
SELECT customer_id, first_order_at
FROM customers;

COMMON MISTAKE

SELECT * returns every column, including ones the task did not ask for. A checked answer must return exactly the requested columns, in the requested order.

Project brief
The project

You support the commercial manager of a UK online gift wholesaler.

Sales for 2011 look lower than 2010. The manager wants to know whether trading really weakened, which departments drove the change, how much value is lost to cancellations, and how much of the business can be traced to known customers.

Your question

Is trading weaker in 2011 than in 2010, where does the change come from, and what should the commercial team look at first?

Before you start

Filtering · Aggregation · Joins · CASE expressions · Dates

Begin project →
What you’ll deliver

A short commercial review with three connected findings, two prioritized follow-up actions and the limits of what invoices can show.

Your data

Retail: two years of real invoice lines (December 2009 to 9 December 2011) for a sample of customers, with products, departments, customers and their regions. Sale invoices and cancellation invoices are both recorded; cancellation lines carry negative quantities.

Your investigations
Size sales and cancellations

Across all invoices, how many sale and cancellation invoices are there, what are gross sales, cancelled value and net sales, and what share of gross sales was cancelled?

Compare 2011 with 2010 by month

For each month from January to November, what were sale-invoice sales in 2010 and in 2011, and by what percentage did 2011 change?

Find the departments behind the change

For January–November of each year, what were sale-invoice sales by department in 2010 and 2011, and which departments changed most?

Check who the 2011 sales come from

For sale invoices from January to November 2011, how many customers and how much of sales come from each region, and from anonymous invoices?
